question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.03(1), on what basis may the Real Estate Examining Board grant a broker's or salesperson's license to an applicant?
choice_a: Only after satisfactory proof of the applicant's competence to safeguard the interests of the public has been presented to the board
choice_b: After the applicant pays the licensing fee, regardless of competence
choice_c: After the applicant obtains a sponsoring broker's signature
choice_d: After the applicant establishes 40 years of continuous Wisconsin residency
explanation: Section 452.03(1) states the board may grant a license only to a person competent to transact the business in a manner that safeguards the public, and only after satisfactory proof of competence has been presented to the board.

question: Which of the following individuals does NOT need a broker's or salesperson's license under Wis. Stat. 452.03(2)?
choice_a: A person who negotiates real estate sales for compensation
choice_b: An individual who, on behalf of a firm or licensee, provides services limited to purely administrative, clerical, or personal duties
choice_c: A person who advertises property for sale on behalf of an owner
choice_d: A person who acts temporarily as a salesperson for a single transaction
explanation: Section 452.03(2) exempts an individual who, on behalf of and under the direction of a firm or licensee, provides services that are limited to those purely administrative, clerical, or personal in nature; section 452.03(1) otherwise requires a license even for temporary or occasional acts.

question: When a business entity submits a license application under Wis. Stat. 452.09(1)(b), what must the application include besides the entity's own name and address?
choice_a: The entity's annual gross revenue
choice_b: The entity's federal tax identification number
choice_c: The name and address of each business representative, and the license number of each business representative licensed as a broker
choice_d: A list of all properties currently under contract
explanation: Section 452.09(1)(b) requires that if the applicant is a business entity, the application include the name and address of each business representative and the license number of each business representative licensed as a broker.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.09(1)(d), an applicant's license application must describe the business or occupation engaged in by the applicant for what minimum period preceding the date of the application?
choice_a: 6 months
choice_b: 1 year
choice_c: 18 months
choice_d: 2 years
explanation: Section 452.09(1)(d) requires disclosure of the business or occupation engaged in by the applicant (or each business representative, if a business entity) for a period of at least 2 years immediately preceding the date of the application.

question: A salesperson applicant who has not completed the board-approved educational program may still have that requirement waived under Wis. Stat. 452.09(2)(a) upon proof of what?
choice_a: Receipt of 10 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law from an accredited institution of higher education
choice_b: Receipt of 20 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law
choice_c: Two years of unlicensed clerical experience in a real estate office
choice_d: Passage of the broker's examination
explanation: Section 452.09(2)(a) allows the board to waive the salesperson educational program requirement upon proof that the applicant has received 10 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law courses from an accredited institution of higher education.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.09(2)(d), the board may waive the broker applicant's business management education requirement upon proof of what?
choice_a: 10 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law
choice_b: 20 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law courses from an accredited institution of higher education, or that the applicant is licensed to practice law in this state
choice_c: Completion of 40 experience points as a salesperson
choice_d: A letter of recommendation from a supervising broker
explanation: Section 452.09(2)(d) permits the board to waive the requirements under par. (c) upon proof of 20 academic credits in real estate or real estate related law courses from an accredited institution, or that the applicant is licensed to practice law in Wisconsin.

question: Wis. Stat. 452.09(3)(a) requires the board to obtain proof that a broker's or salesperson's applicant has a fair understanding of the general purposes and legal effect of which of the following?
choice_a: Federal fair housing regulations exclusively
choice_b: Local zoning ordinances exclusively
choice_c: Deeds, mortgages, land contracts of sale, leases, bills of sale, and conditional sales contracts
choice_d: Environmental impact statements
explanation: Section 452.09(3)(a) requires proof of a fair understanding of the general purposes and general legal effect of deeds, mortgages, land contracts of sale, leases, bills of sale, and conditional sales contracts, as well as of the obligations between principal and agent.

question: How does the board determine competency under Wis. Stat. 452.09(3)(b) for an applicant who is unable to write because of a physical handicap?
choice_a: The applicant is automatically exempted from any competency determination
choice_b: The applicant must submit a medical waiver in lieu of examination
choice_c: The applicant must be examined by a licensed physician instead of the board
choice_d: The board determines competency by means of only an oral examination
explanation: Section 452.09(3)(b) provides that the board shall determine competency by means of only an oral examination for any applicant who is unable to write because of a physical handicap.

question: Except as otherwise provided, Wis. Stat. 452.09(3)(d) states the board may not grant a broker's license unless the applicant does what?
choice_a: Passes both the salesperson's examination and the broker's examination, and meets the experience requirements
choice_b: Passes the broker's examination only
choice_c: Passes the salesperson's examination only, since broker-level knowledge is presumed included
choice_d: Submits three letters of reference from licensed brokers
explanation: Section 452.09(3)(d) states that, except as provided under s. 452.12(2) or a reciprocal agreement, the board may not grant a broker's license unless the applicant passes both the salesperson's examination and the broker's examination and meets the experience requirements under sub. (4).

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.09(4)(a)1, an individual applicant for a broker's license must submit evidence of having practiced as a licensed salesperson under the direct supervision of a licensed broker for what period?
choice_a: At least 1 year within the last 2 years
choice_b: At least 2 years within the last 4 years preceding the date of the application
choice_c: At least 3 years within the last 5 years
choice_d: At least 5 continuous years
explanation: Section 452.09(4)(a)1 requires evidence that the applicant has practiced as a licensed salesperson under the direct supervision of a licensed broker for at least 2 years within the last 4 years preceding the date of the broker's license application.

question: An individual applicant for a broker's license has closed 3 residential transactions (5 points each) and 1 commercial transaction (10 points) while working as a supervised licensed salesperson. Using the point system in Wis. Stat. 452.09(4)(a)2, how many points has the applicant earned toward the 40-point experience requirement?
choice_a: 15 points
choice_b: 20 points
choice_c: 25 points
choice_d: 40 points
explanation: Under the point system, each completed residential transaction is worth 5 points (3 x 5 = 15) and each completed commercial transaction is worth 10 points (1 x 10 = 10), for a total of 25 points, which is short of the 40-point requirement.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.09(4)(b), an applicant who is licensed to practice law in Wisconsin may satisfy the broker's license experience requirement by submitting what?
choice_a: Evidence of a current certificate of financial responsibility under s. 101.654
choice_b: Evidence of 40 points under the standard point system
choice_c: Evidence of 2 years' licensure as a broker in another state
choice_d: Evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant has experience related to real estate
explanation: Section 452.09(4)(b) allows an applicant licensed to practice law in Wisconsin to satisfy the experience requirement by submitting evidence satisfactory to the board that the applicant has experience related to real estate.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.09(4)(d), a nonresident applicant for a broker's license may satisfy the experience requirement, absent a reciprocal agreement, by showing what?
choice_a: The applicant has been a licensed broker under the laws of another state for at least 2 years within the last 4 years preceding the application
choice_b: The applicant has resided in Wisconsin for at least 1 year
choice_c: The applicant has completed 20 academic credits in real estate law
choice_d: The applicant holds a certificate of financial responsibility under s. 101.654
explanation: Section 452.09(4)(d) allows a nonresident broker applicant, except as provided in a reciprocal agreement, to satisfy the experience requirement by showing licensure as a broker under the laws of another state for at least 2 years within the last 4 years preceding the application.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.10(1), if a license application is made by a business entity, who must verify the application?
choice_a: Any licensed salesperson employed by the entity
choice_b: A business representative who is a licensed individual broker or a licensed broker business entity and is acting as the entity's business representative
choice_c: The entity's registered agent for service of process
choice_d: A notary public with no affiliation to the entity
explanation: Section 452.10(1) requires that an application made by a business entity be verified by a business representative that is a licensed individual broker or a licensed broker business entity acting as a business representative for the entity.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.10(2)(a), a new application for a license shall be for what period?
choice_a: A full new 2-year term starting from the date the license is granted
choice_b: A 1-year probationary term
choice_c: The remainder of the biennial license period
choice_d: A 4-year term matching the applicant's education certification
explanation: Section 452.10(2)(a) states that each new application for a license shall be for the remainder of the biennial license period.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.10(2)(b), when is part of an application fee returned to the applicant?
choice_a: Whenever the applicant fails the competency examination
choice_b: Whenever the applicant is denied a license for any reason
choice_c: Fees are never returned under any circumstance
choice_d: When the application is withdrawn in writing before the board has made any investigation
explanation: Section 452.10(2)(b) provides that unless an application is withdrawn in writing before the board has made any investigation, no part of the fee shall be returned.

question: Wis. Stat. 452.11(3) requires every nonresident applicant, and every resident licensee who becomes a nonresident, to file with the board what?
choice_a: An irrevocable consent that actions may be commenced against the applicant or licensee in the proper Wisconsin court by service of process on the board or an authorized employee
choice_b: A cash bond equal to one year's projected commissions
choice_c: A sworn statement renouncing licensure in their home state
choice_d: Proof of Wisconsin property ownership
explanation: Section 452.11(3) requires a nonresident applicant or licensee to file an irrevocable consent that actions may be commenced against them in the proper court of the Wisconsin county where the cause of action arises or the plaintiff resides, by service of process on the board or a duly authorized employee.

question: Under Wis. Stat. 452.11(4), how many days must elapse after mailing of process or pleading to a nonresident licensee before a default judgment may be taken?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: 20 days
choice_c: 30 days
choice_d: 60 days
explanation: Section 452.11(4) states that no judgment by default may be taken in any action or proceeding within 20 days after the date of mailing the process or pleading to the nonresident licensee.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.01(2), within how many business days after a completed application is received must the board review and make a determination on an original license application?
choice_a: 30 business days
choice_b: 45 business days
choice_c: 60 business days
choice_d: 90 business days
explanation: REEB 12.01(2) requires the board to review and make a determination on an original application for a license within 60 business days after a completed application is received by the department.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.01(5), before acting on a new application from a previously licensed applicant, what must the applicant furnish, absent a board waiver?
choice_a: A new set of fingerprints
choice_b: A newly executed reciprocal agreement
choice_c: Proof of current employment with a licensed broker
choice_d: Sufficient proof that the applicant has not acted as a salesperson or broker since the applicant's license expired
explanation: REEB 12.01(5) provides that no action shall be taken on a new application from a previously licensed applicant until the applicant furnishes sufficient proof that the applicant has not acted as a salesperson or broker since the license expired, though the board may waive this requirement.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.01(7), no action may be taken on a new broker's or salesperson's license application unless the applicant is at least what age?
choice_a: 18 years old
choice_b: 16 years old
choice_c: 19 years old
choice_d: 21 years old
explanation: REEB 12.01(7) states that no action shall be taken on any new application for a broker's or salesperson's license unless the applicant is 18 years of age or over.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.011, an individual seeking a criminal conviction predetermination must pay a fee of $68.00. How may this fee later be used?
choice_a: It is fully refunded if the board determines the applicant is not disqualified
choice_b: It may be applied to the license application fee if the individual applies for a real estate license within 1 year of the predetermination decision
choice_c: It may be applied toward the continuing education fee for the next renewal
choice_d: It is forfeited entirely and can never be applied to any future fee
explanation: REEB 12.011(1)(am) sets the predetermination fee at $68.00, and REEB 12.011(1m) allows that fee to be applied to the application fee under REEB 12.01(4) if the individual applies for a broker or salesperson license within 1 year of the determination decision.

question: Among the factors the board must consider in making a criminal conviction predetermination under REEB 12.011(3), which is listed in the rule?
choice_a: The applicant's current credit score
choice_b: The applicant's marital status at the time of conviction
choice_c: The applicant's activities since the conviction, including employment, education, participation in treatment, and payment of restitution as evidence of rehabilitation
choice_d: Whether the applicant has family members who are already licensed
explanation: REEB 12.011(3)(f) directs the board to consider the individual's activities since the conviction, including employment, education, participation in treatment, payment of restitution, and any other evidence of rehabilitation.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.012(2), an applicant for reciprocal licensure as a service member, former service member, or spouse must submit which of the following, among other items?
choice_a: Proof of at least 40 experience points under the standard point system
choice_b: A Wisconsin law license
choice_c: Evidence of passing the Wisconsin broker's examination
choice_d: A statement that the applicant resides in Wisconsin, plus evidence of holding a license in good standing from a jurisdiction outside Wisconsin
explanation: REEB 12.012(2) requires such applicants to submit, among other things, a statement that the applicant resides in Wisconsin and evidence of holding a license in good standing granted by a governmental authority outside Wisconsin that qualifies the individual to perform the corresponding acts.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.025(3), what action(s) may the board take against an applicant who cheats on a licensing examination?
choice_a: Withholding the applicant's score, entering a failing score, and/or suspending the applicant's ability to sit for the next scheduled examination
choice_b: Automatic permanent disqualification from ever taking the exam again
choice_c: Referral for criminal prosecution only
choice_d: A monetary fine paid directly to the department, with no effect on the exam score
explanation: REEB 12.025(3) states that an action for cheating may include withholding the applicant's score, entering a failing score, and suspending the applicant's ability to sit for the next scheduled examination, with the action related to the seriousness of the offense.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.04(2m)(a), a licensee whose license has been expired for more than 5 years generally may do what?
choice_a: Reapply for the license using the standard initial application process
choice_b: Not reapply for the license using the initial application process
choice_c: Automatically have the license reinstated upon fee payment
choice_d: Apply only for a reciprocal license, regardless of prior Wisconsin credential
explanation: REEB 12.04(2m)(a) states that a licensee with an expired license may not reapply for the license using the initial application process, and instead must meet the education, examination, and experience requirements specified for renewal more than 5 years after expiration.

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code REEB 12.04(3)(b), when may a licensee seeking reinstatement (after revocation, surrender, or failing to renew within 5 years) resume practicing real estate?
choice_a: Immediately upon filing the reinstatement application
choice_b: After completing continuing education, even before board action
choice_c: Not until the board grants reinstatement of the license
choice_d: After 90 days have passed from the date of filing
explanation: REEB 12.04(3)(b) provides that a licensee may not practice real estate prior to being granted reinstatement of the license.
